newsitem.title: GABON: Chad president leaves Gabon, Mobutu possibly later.
newsitem.headline: Chad president leaves Gabon, Mobutu possibly later.

text.p: The presidents of Chad and Congo left Gabon on Friday after a mini-summit on Zaire and Gabonese officials said that President Mobutu Sese Seko would probably leave later in the day.
Officials in Kinshasa said on Thursday that Mobutu, who is fighting cancer and Laurent Kabila's rebels, would return to his capital on Friday -- unless there were other talks.
Gabonese officials said that still appeared to be the plan. "In principle, (he leaves) this evening but that is not yet certain," one said.

Zaire's information minister, Kin-Kiey Mulumba, said on Thursday that Mobutu would return on Friday. "He is coming back after the summit, unless there is another meeting," he told Radio France International.
The information minister has rejected suggestions that Mobutu's departure for Gabon was a veiled flight into exile. "There is no reason why the president should flee the country, no reason."

Mobutu and Gabon's President Omar Bongo, another veteran African leader, met the presidents of Chad, Congo, the Central African Republic and former Spanish colony Equatorial Guinea at the presidential palace.
Cameroon, chairman of the Organisation of African Unity, sent its foreign minister.

Gabon's government newspaper, l'Union, said the presidents of Chad, Congo, Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea would leave on Friday. It made no mention of Mobutu. Witnesses reported the departure of Chad's President Idriss Deby and Congo's Pascal Lissouba.
